result.title: Preface
result.summary: The Police Retirement System of St. Louis (PRS-STL) issued an RFP on February 2, 2024, for actuarial auditing services. Proposals were due March 8, 2024, at 4:00 p.m. CDT, with an award expected within 60 days. Interested firms were asked to submit company and representative contact details and email the cover page to PRS@stlouisprs.org for updates. The Board of Trustees will review proposals and negotiate competitively, selecting the best-qualified respondent. Established in 1957 under Missouri law, PRS-STL serves more than 3,000 members, retirees, survivors, and beneficiaries, providing retirement, disability, death, and cost-of-living benefits. It seeks one firm to replicate the assumptions, methods, calculations, and experience in its September 30, 2023 valuation; Cheiron, Inc. is its current actuary. The audit covers actuarial standards, assumptions and disclosures, methodology, contribution rates, prior-valuation changes, government reporting, plan summaries, experience-study demographics, and benefit calculations. The RFP lists relevant statutes and historical audit, valuation, and GASB materials, and covers proposal requirements, schedule, evaluation, selection, conditions, contract award, and a questionnaire.

result.title: A. Minimum Audit Subject Matter:
result.summary: The audit covers the appropriateness of actuarial assumptions and reserve accounts; compliance of assumptions and methods with regulations, policies, recognized actuarial principles, standards of practice, professional conduct, and qualification standards; accuracy of funding calculations, including service-credit portability; and validation of the September 30, 2023 fiscal-year valuation using a model or sampling based on Cheiron, Inc.’s data, methods, and assumptions. It also evaluates test results, reconciles significant differences between the auditor’s and Cheiron’s findings and calculations, and assesses compliance with required disclosures, including GASB standards.

result.title: B. Completed Audit and Review Report Content:
result.summary: The completed audit report must assess valuation accuracy and reasonableness, liabilities, costs, required contributions, experience-study findings, assumptions, and cost methodology; recommend any alternative assumptions or report improvements; and compare existing methods and assumptions with the replicative audit. Proposals must be sealed, delivered to the specified PRS-STL address, and include one original, four exact copies, and a USB PDF; email/fax submissions are excluded. Deadline: 4:00 p.m. CST, March 8, 2024. Responses must describe services and schedule commitment; firm and assigned staff qualifications, turnover, minority participation, and recent audited firms; hourly rates, estimated hours, maximum fee including expenses; qualifications, three similar-service references, licenses, bonding, and required insurance limits with PRS-STL as additional insured. The auditor must be independent and disclose City-related work. An authorized officer must sign. Duplicate company proposals require selection of one or all are rejected. Contract is one-time, with a renewal option; tax and license compliance proof is required at award.

result.title: C. Proposed Actuarial Auditing Methods
result.summary:
C. Proposed Actuarial Auditing Methods
1. Provide an estimated timeline for completion of the work that includes each stage of the process. Be sure to include a time estimate for information or data gathering required from the PRS-STL and/or its current consulting actuary. Indicate points in the audit and review when your firm plans to interact with PRS-STL staff at the PRS- STL office.
2. Describe your firm’s approach to recommendations regarding the amortization of unfunded liabilities.
3. Describe your approach to measuring funded status and funding progress in order to facilitate the assessment of trends over several valuations for a client.
4. Describe your quality control processes for actuarial audit reports and recommendations. How are these services monitored and reviewed?
5. Provide an example of one recent actuarial audit report for current or former client.

result.title: D. Mandatory Minimum Qualifications
result.summary: As of the response due date, firms must have at least five years of experience providing actuarial valuations, experience studies, audits, and pension consulting for public plans, plus supervising-actuary experience with major retirement systems, particularly large cost-sharing systems. The principal actuary must have at least five years of professional experience, be an enrolled actuary, an American Academy of Actuaries member, and a Society of Actuaries Associate (Fellowship preferred), and have at least five years’ experience testifying before legislative or administrative bodies on actuarial positions or costs of proposed legislation. Firms must not unreasonably limit liability for negligence, hold required permits and licenses, maintain $1 million in liability and professional errors-and-omissions insurance when proposals are submitted and throughout the agreement, and provide their own facilities, equipment, supplies, and support staff.

result.summary:

result.title: F. Question and Answer Period / Contact Information
result.summary: RFP questions must be emailed to the Police Retirement System of St. Louis Executive Director at PRS@stlouisprs.org by 4:00 p.m. CST, February 16, 2024; answers will be summarized and posted at www.stlouisprs.org. Contact with other PRS-STL trustees or employees is prohibited. Trustees will review proposals after the deadline; the highest-ranked respondent will receive contact instructions, but selection is tentative pending contract negotiation and Board approval. PRS-STL may negotiate any proposal aspect. The tentative schedule is: RFP issued February 2; questions due February 16; answers posted February 23; bids due March 8 by 4:00 p.m. CST; selected-bidder presentations April 8; evaluation completed April 24; intent to award May 29. PRS-STL may change the schedule. Evaluation considers completeness, timeliness, relevant public-pension experience, qualifications and technical competence, written and oral presentation quality, innovation, past performance, resources, and other proposal or interview matters. A shortlist will be formed, and the Actuarial Audit Services Committee may interview firms and request presentations to itself or the Board.

result.title: VII. SELECTION PROCESS
result.summary: After receiving input from the Actuarial Audit Services Committee, the PRS-STL Board of Trustees will review proposals and may rate and select a respondent immediately or schedule interviews and/or another selection meeting. Interviews, if held, assess presentation quality, work program and schedule, deadline performance, client communication and reporting, and team management; no additional handouts, including PowerPoint materials, are allowed. At the selection meeting, proposals are evaluated on key team members’ roles and experience, the approach to managing the actuarial auditor role, qualifications and background, and ability to ask and answer questions. Each Trustee ranks respondents; the respondent with the lowest cumulative ranking total is deemed best qualified to negotiate a contract. All proposers are notified of the outcome, and the PRS-STL website identifies the selected respondent. If contract terms cannot be agreed, negotiations may be offered to the next-ranked respondent, and so on.

result.title: VIII. GENERAL CONDITIONS
result.summary: PRS-STL may reject proposals, waive irregularities, select based on its best interests, cancel or revise the RFP, seek information, negotiate, interview respondents, and establish further criteria; no award or purchase is binding until a fully approved written contract. Respondents bear all costs, must meet deadlines, monitor addenda, comply with applicable laws, and confirm their ability to perform. Proposals may be amended or withdrawn before the deadline under stated procedures; submissions become PRS-STL property and may become public. Respondents accept the RFP, authorize verification inquiries, waive challenges, and release and indemnify PRS-STL and related parties; misrepresentations may disqualify them. Team changes require approval. Contracts require nondiscrimination, ADA compliance, federal work-authorization certification, acceptable insurance, and contractor indemnification; Missouri law and St. Louis venue apply. PRS-STL may terminate with 30 days’ notice. Auditors may inspect records during the contract and for five years afterward. Firms certify prices are independent and disclose no disqualifying conflicts.

result.title: IX. CONTRACT AWARD
result.summary: PRS-STL may award to the most advantageous qualified proposal, make no award, negotiate with respondents, reject proposals, award without clarification, split the contract among multiple firms, or approach the next qualified respondent if contracting with the selected firm fails. The Board of Trustees has final approval discretion. The questionnaire requests respondent contact details and firm information: business, actuarial-service history, ownership and planned changes, public and total defined-benefit clients, valuation systems and hardware, available actuaries’ credentials and experience, key staff and resources, litigation, disciplinary history, conflicts, and a sample monthly invoice. It also invites other relevant information; asks about public-system actuarial and audit experience, a sample audit report, and at least three recent comparable client references; and requests understanding of project requirements, methodology, work and management plans, and a schedule with input/output milestones. FY2023 valuation reports are expected by late February 2024. Respondents must return the completed questionnaire with their proposal.
